overview.headline: DNA stores hereditary information in a double helix

keyPoints.point: Students learn that DNA is the hereditary material found in humans and almost all other organisms.
keyPoints.quote: DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, is the hereditary material in humans and almost all other organisms.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that most DNA is located in the cell nucleus as nuclear DNA.
keyPoints.quote: Most DNA is located in the cell nucleus (where it is called nuclear DNA)

keyPoints.point: Students learn that information in DNA is stored as a code made up of four chemical bases.
keyPoints.quote: The information in DNA is stored as a code made up of four chemical bases: adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), and thymine (T).

keyPoints.point: Students learn how DNA bases pair to form units called base pairs for the ladder structure.
keyPoints.quote: DNA bases pair up with each other, A with T and C with G, to form units called base pairs.

keyTerms.gloss: DNA located in the cell nucleus that holds most hereditary information
keyTerms.quote: Most DNA is located in the cell nucleus (where it is called nuclear DNA)

keyTerms.gloss: Small amount of DNA found in mitochondria that helps convert energy from food
keyTerms.quote: but a small amount of DNA can also be found in the mitochondria (where it is called mitochondrial DNA or mtDNA).

keyTerms.gloss: Units formed when adenine pairs with thymine and cytosine pairs with guanine
keyTerms.quote: DNA bases pair up with each other, A with T and C with G, to form units called base pairs.

keyTerms.gloss: Structure made from a base, sugar and phosphate linked together
keyTerms.quote: Together, a base, sugar, and phosphate are called a nucleotide.

keyTerms.gloss: Spiral shape formed by two long strands of nucleotides
keyTerms.quote: Nucleotides are arranged in two long strands that form a spiral called a double helix.
